_format: skill-creator eval format. Run each prompt in a fresh session with and without the skill; grade the assertions. expect_trigger false marks a should-not-trigger probe.

evals.prompt: Make a 60 second motion graphics explainer for our product aimed at finance people. Calm, not hypey. We'll add a voice later.
assertions: Writes or asks for the script first and gets the owner's OK on the words before rendering
Uses one idea per line and a calm pace, with the cut driven by the words (about 2.45 words a second), not a fixed scene length
Marks anything not yet built as planned on screen and labels any comparison as an illustration rather than a measurement
Opens on a question or pain specific to finance roles (for example unplanned spend) rather than a product feature
Plans a music-only render first, with the voice-over added later as a separate -voice version

evals.prompt: I have ElevenLabs credits. How do I get these videos voiced without burning everything on bad takes?
assertions: Generates per subtitle line rather than one long take per video
Starts with the shortest opening hook per voice as a test and lets the owner listen before anything else
Uses dry runs (no --go), a credit cap, and caching so a line is never paid twice
Mentions that free plans cannot use library voices through the API and that free-plan audio is non-commercial
Keeps the API key out of files and chat (environment variable or OS keyring)

evals.prompt: My batch script renders the first video fine and then the rest of the queue just silently finishes without rendering anything. It's a bash while read loop calling ffmpeg.
assertions: Identifies that ffmpeg reads stdin and consumes the loop's input
Fixes it with -nostdin (or redirecting ffmpeg's stdin from /dev/null)
Does not blame the video files or suggest re-encoding them

evals.prompt: Re-render the founder video with the new scene, same file name is fine.
assertions: Keeps the existing rendered video: moves it aside into an older folder or renders under a new name instead of overwriting it
Checks the changed scene with stills or a contact sheet before the full render

evals.prompt: Trim the first 3 seconds off this mp4 and convert it to a gif.
assertions: Answers with a direct ffmpeg command and does not invoke the seekframe skill or its rendering pipeline
